On evaluation itself, the position saved is that two reviewers scoring the same eval rubric still land three points apart [2]. You decided to drop LangChain in favour of direct Anthropic SDK calls for tool loops [1]. The reason recorded is that the agent abstraction layer was making tool-call debugging significantly harder [2], and direct calls make streaming and error handling explicit instead of hidden [3].

Seed rounds at this stage are landing between three and five million on fifteen post [1], with median dilution holding around twenty percent through the last two quarters [2]. Funds expect that round to buy eighteen to twenty four months of runway [3].

Referrals from the first five engineers produced every good hire so far [1], and take-home exercises lose candidates who already hold competing offers [2]. Pair programming on real code predicts performance better than algorithm puzzles [3].

You decided a single paid tier converts better than three tiers at this stage [1]. The reasoning saved is that usage-based pricing punishes the power users who evangelise the product hardest [2], and anchoring on seat price makes the product feel like team software rather than personal software [3].

Users who save their first item within five minutes retain at twice the rate [1]. Removing the signup wall before the first action lifted activation noticeably [2], and the empty state is now doing more onboarding work than the product tour ever did [3].
